text:
Daily Kos Staff

Poor Jay Clayton.

Wednesday was supposed to be his big day: a Senate confirmation hearing where he would transition from being the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York to the director of National Intelligence.

But then President Donald Trump stepped in and whisked it all away, delaying Clayton’s hearing so that he could lean on Congress to vote for an entirely unrelated bill—the SAVE Act—and to force the Senate to confirm Clayton’s proposed replacement, James McDonald.

Trump went on Truth Social early Wednesday to complain that Congress was moving too fast to confirm Clayton.

Come again?

It’s super-weird for Trump to be lashing out at Republicans for speeding through his own nominee. But, of course, it’s actually the fault of Democrats somehow.

“The Republicans agreed with Dumocrats to remove very fair, and talented, William Pulte, from serving as Acting DNI in return for getting FISA approved by the Dumocrats. However, the Republicans moved so fast with the hearings of the Great Jay Clayton, current U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, that Pulte would be gone before the Dumocrats would vote on FISA. Now, the Dumocrats are saying they will vote against FISA—So, the Republicans wound up having fulfilled their commitment, but Democrats broke the Deal,” he ranted.

Of course, there was never any such deal.

Sure, Democrats refused to vote in favor of the bill to extend the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, or FISA, as pushback against the nomination of Bill Pulte, but that was in no way some promise that Democrats would shift to voting “yes” if his nomination got pulled.

To the extent that there was any “deal” that existed outside of Trump’s tattered brain, it was that the Democrats would vote to confirm Clayton swiftly to head off Pulte becoming acting director of National Intelligence on Friday, once Tulsi Gabbard leaves.

Related | Why Trump keeps appointing temporary flunkies

But let’s pretend that there was actually a deal with the Democrats to pass FISA if Trump kicked Pulte to the curb. What does that have to do with Trump’s attempt to reshape and corrupt elections with his SAVE Act? The issue with that bill is that Trump doesn’t have the votes.

The Republican votes, that is.

The GOP keeps forcing votes on SAVE, and in its last attempt, it couldn’t even muster a simple majority because Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, and Thom Tillis of North Carolina joined Democrats in rejecting attaching it to the immigration funding bill.

That came after two other attempts that also floundered because not enough Republicans would back it.

Delaying Clayton’s hearing also means that Pulte becomes acting DNI once Gabbard leaves on Friday.

It’s becoming increasingly clear that Trump wants Pulte as DNI but knows he can’t get him confirmed. He’s even been bragging about how Democrats won’t confirm Pulte because they are wusses.

“Why are they afraid of this guy? I mean, they’re so afraid of him, they’ll do anything not to have pulled to go in there. He’s a very capable guy, and they’re worried about that,” Trump said.

As with the SAVE Act, Trump seems to have forgotten—or just ignored—that Pulte’s nomination didn’t falter because of Democrats. It’s because GOP Sens. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, Collins, and Murkowski crossed the aisle. Democrats don’t hold a majority and are unable to block Trump nominees even if they vote in lockstep—it’s his own party that decided tanked the nomination.

It’s also increasingly clear that Trump has a suspicion that McDonald, his pick to replace Clayton, can’t be confirmed either, which is why he’s holding Congress hostage.

What’s the problem with McDonald? Perhaps the fact that he’s still one of Trump’s personal lawyers, representing him in his endless attempts to make his New York felony convictions go away.

Compromising national security as leverage to get a bill that Trump’s own party can’t pass is … a choice. But Trump is going to keep resorting to these sorts of shenanigans because even his own party appears to have its limits.

It isn’t the job of Democrats to rescue Trump’s terrible bills—no matter how much Trump whines about it. Sucks to be you, dude.
